questions.question: What is the LCM of 120 and 450?
questions.solution:
We can write,

⇒ 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5

⇒ 450 = 2 × 3² × 5²

LCM of two numbers is computed by taking the highest powers of all the factors

∴ LCM of 120 and 450 = 2³ × 3² × 5² = 1800

The average of four consecutive odd numbers is 40. What is the largest number?
questions.solution:
Let the odd numbers be x, (x + 2), (x + 4), (x + 6)

Average of numbers = (x + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6)/4 = 40

⇒ 4x + 12 = 160

⇒ 4x = 148

⇒ x = 148/4 = 37

∴ Largest number = x + 6 = 37 + 6 = 43

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (5, 3) in the line y = -2?
questions.solution:
When a point is reflected about the x-axis, the x-coordinate remains the same and only the y-coordinate is transformed

∵ The line y = -2 is parallel to the x-axis, x-coordinate will remain the same after reflection

Now, along the y-direction, the distance between the reflected point and the line will be equal to the distance between the original point and the line

⇒ Distance between point and line along y-direction = |3 - (-2)| = |5| = 5 unit

⇒ Y-coordinate of reflection = -2 - 5 = -7

∴ The reflection point is (5, -7)

questions.question: The distance between the points (4, 8) and (k, -4) is 13. What is the value of k?
questions.solution:
According to the distance formula, the distance between two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) can be computed as,

Distance = √[(x₂ – x₁)² + (y₂ – y₁)²]

Given, distance between the points (4, 8) and (k, -4) is 13

⇒ (13)² = (k – 4)² + (–4 – 8)²

⇒ 169 = k² + 16 – 8k + 144

⇒ k² – 8k – 9 = 0

⇒ k² – 9k + k – 9 = 0

⇒ k(k – 9) + 1(k – 9) = 0

⇒ (k – 9) (k + 1) = 0

⇒ k = 9, -1

∴ Value of k = -1

questions.question: The 3rd and 8th term of an arithmetic progression are -14 and 1 respectively. What is the 11th term?
questions.solution:
The nth term of an AP with first term ‘a’ and difference ‘d’ = a + (n – 1)d

3rd term = a + 2d = -14 ----(1)

8th term = a + 7d = 1 ----(2)

Subtracting (1) from (2), we get,

⇒ a + 7d – a – 2d = 1 + 14

⇒ 5d = 15

⇒ d = 3

Substituting in (2),

⇒ a = 1 – 21 = -20

∴ 11th term = a + 10d = -20 + 10(3) = -20 + 30 = 10

questions.question: If cos θ = 35/37, then what is the value of cot θ?
questions.solution:
Using trigonometric identities,

sin² θ = 1 – cos² θ = 1 – (35/37)² = 144/1369

⇒ sin θ = √(144/1369) = 12/37

∴ cot θ = cos θ/sin θ = (35/37)/(12/37) = 35/12

questions.question: If a person walks at 12 km/hr instead of 10 km/hr, he would have walked 1 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance (in kms) travelled by him at 10 km/hr in the same time?
questions.solution:
Let the actual distance travelled by him at 10 km/hr be ‘x’ km

Time taken = x/10 hrs.

When the speed is 12 km/hr, distance travelled = (x + 1) km

Time taken = (x + 1)/12

∵ Same time is taken in both cases,

⇒ x/10 = (x + 1)/12

⇒ 12x = 10x + 10

⇒ 2x = 10

⇒ x = 10/2 = 5 km

∴ Actual distance travelled by him = 5 km

questions.question: What is the equation of the line perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = -6 and having Y-intercept 3?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A line is given 2x + 3y = -6

Y-intercept is 3

**Calculations:**

According to the question, we have

A line with slope ‘m’ is represented as: y = mx + c

Given line, 2x + 3y = -6

⇒ y = (-2/3)x – 2

Slope of line = -2/3

The product of the slope of perpendicular lines is -1,

Slope of required line = -1/(-2/3) = 3/2

Equation of line is

⇒ y = (3/2)x + c

Given y-intercept = 3,

Putting x = 0, y = 3,

⇒ 3 = c

⇒ y = (3/2)x + 3

⇒ 2y = 3x + 6

**∴ Equation of required line is 3x – 2y = -6**

questions.question: If 5 employees are transferred from department A to department F, then number of employees in department F would be between those of which two departments?

No. of employees in department A = 17 – 5 = 12

If a wholesaler, sells a tin of coffee at Rs 528 he faces a loss of 12%. Now if he decides to sell it at Rs. 636, what will be the profit (in %)?
questions.solution:
When selling price = Rs. 528, loss = 12%

∵ Cost price – loss = Selling price

⇒ CP – 12% of CP = 528

⇒ 0.88CP = 528

⇒ Cost price = 528/0.88 = Rs. 600

∵ Selling price = Cost price + Profit

∴ When selling price is Rs. 636, profit = [(636 – 600)/600) × 100 = 6%

questions.question: Albert invested an amount of x rupees in a fixed deposit scheme offering 10% per annum for 1st year and 15% per annum for 2ⁿd year and received an amount of Rs. 20,240 after the two years. What is x (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
∵ Simple interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

For first year, Principal = Rs. x, Rate = 10%

Amount after first year = x + (x × 10 × 1)/100 = Rs. 1.1x

For second year, Principal = Rs. 1.1x = Rate = 15%

Amount after second year = 1.1x + (1.1x × 15 × 1)/100 = Rs. 1.265x

⇒ 1.265x = 20240

∴ x = 20240/1.265 = Rs. 16000

questions.question: If A's wealth is 4/9 times of B's and C's is 7/6 times of B's, what is the ratio of C's wealth to A's?
questions.solution:
A’s wealth = 4/9 × (B’s wealth) ----(1)

C’s wealth = 7/6 × (B’s wealth) ----(2)

Dividing (2) by (1),

⇒ C’s wealth/A’s wealth = (7/6)/(4/9) = 21/8

∴ Ratio of C’s wealth to A’s wealth = 21 ∶ 8

questions.question: The discount offered on a Shirt of Rs. 500 and a pair of Trousers of Rs 1000 is 20% and 40% respectively. If Ajay bought 2 Shirt and 3 pair of Trousers then what was the effective discount (in %) he received?
questions.solution:
∵ Selling price = Marked price – Discount

Marked price of 1 shirt = Rs. 500

Selling price of 1 shirt = 500 – 20% of 500 = Rs. 400

Marked price of a pair of trousers = Rs. 1000

Selling price of a pair of trousers = 1000 – 40% of 1000 = Rs. 600

Marked price of 2 shirts and 3 pairs of trousers = 2(500) + 3(1000) = Rs. 4000

Selling price of 2 shirts and 3 pairs of trousers = 2(400) + 3(600) = Rs. 2600

Total discount = 4000 – 2600 = Rs. 1400

∴ Effective discount = (1400/4000) × 100 = 35%

questions.question: A, B and C can do a job working alone in 6, 9 and 18 days respectively. They all work together for 1 day, then A and B quit. How many days C working alone will take to complete the remainder of the job?
questions.solution:
A’s 1 day work = 1/6

B’s 1 day work = 1/9

C’s 1 day work = 1/18

Let C alone worked for ‘x’ days

∵ A and B worked only for one day and C worked for (x + 1) days,

⇒ A’s 1 day work + B’s 1 day work + C’s (x + 1) days’ work = 1

⇒ 1/6 + 1/9 + (x + 1)/18 = 1

⇒ (x + 1)/18 = 13/18

⇒ x + 1 = 13

⇒ x = 13 – 1 = 12

∴ C worked alone for 12 days

questions.question: A man wills 40% of his wealth to his wife and rest to his children. What percent of the wealth willed to the wife do the children get?
questions.solution:
Let the total wealth be ‘x’

Wealth willed to wife = 40% of x = 0.4x

Wealth for children = x – 0.4x = 0.6x

∴ Required percentage = (0.6x/0.4x) × 100 = 150%

What is the diameter (in cm) of a sphere of surface area 6.16 sq cm?
questions.solution:
Surface area of a sphere with radius ‘r’ = 4πr²

Given, surface area = 6.16 sq. cm

⇒ 4πr² = 6.16

⇒ r² = 0.49

⇒ r = √0.49 = 0.7 cm

∴ Diameter of sphere = 2r = 2(0.7) = 1.4 cm
